plainTitle: New 9-storey long-term care home approved at 60 Guildwood Parkway

sources.label: Staff report from the Director, Community Planning, Scarborough District

whatIsProposed.text: City Council changed the Official Plan and the zoning rules for 60 Guildwood Parkway so that a 9-storey long-term care home can be built there.

citations.quote: to permit a 9-storey long-term care facility at 60 Guildwood Parkway
City Council amend the Official Plan for the lands municipally known as 60 Guildwood Parkway

whatIsProposed.text: The new home would replace a one-storey long-term care home on the site. The number of resident rooms would go from 169 to 512.

citations.quote: The subject lands are currently occupied by a one-storey long-term care home consisting of 169 long-term care rooms and a surface parking lot.
The proposed long-term care home includes a total of 512 long-term care resident rooms

whatIsProposed.text: The plan has 149 surface parking spaces and 88 bicycle parking spaces. Cars would enter from two driveways on Guildwood Parkway.

citations.quote: A total of 149 vehicular parking spaces
A total of 88 bicycle parking spaces
proposed via two accesses on Guildwood Parkway

whatIsProposed.text: The land is changed from an area for low-rise homes to an area for institutions such as schools and health care. A special policy limits the site to a long-term care home.

citations.quote: redesignate the subject lands from Neighbourhoods to Institutional Areas
a Site and Area Specific Policy will scope the permitted uses to a long-term care facility

why.text: Low-rise areas usually allow buildings up to four storeys, or six on major streets like Guildwood Parkway. A 9-storey building needed the change.

citations.quote: Generally the Neighbourhoods designation provides for buildings up to four storeys in height.
permit 6 storey residential development on lands designated Neighbourhoods fronting on Major Streets like Guildwood Parkway

why.text: City staff supported the plan. They said the site's large size, shape and slope make the height work, and that it is near Kingston Road and a planned rapid transit line.
why.caveat: This is the opinion of City staff. The community council did not endorse it (see the steps below).

citations.quote: staff finds the redesignation of the property to Institutional Areas to be appropriate due to the property's distinct size, shape, and location
within 400 metres of Kingston Road and the future Scarborough East Rapid Transit Line

why.text: Staff said the area needs more long-term care beds. The share of local residents over 64 grew from 15% in 2016 to 16.4% in 2021.

citations.quote: providing much needed additional long-term care beds to support the needs of Toronto's growing and aging population
identified 16.4% of residents over the age of 64 years, an increase from the 15% from the 2016 census

whoIsAffected.text: The site is on the north side of Guildwood Parkway, west of Livingston Road, in Ward 24 (Scarborough-Guildwood).

citations.quote: The site is an irregularly shaped corner lot located on the north side of Guildwood Parkway, west of Livingston Road.

whoIsAffected.text: Neighbours to the east and north: the building would be about 24.5 metres from the townhouses to the east and about 15.9 metres from the nearest houses to the north.

citations.quote: an approximately 24.5 metre setback from the townhouses to the east, as well as an approximately 15.9 metre setback from the nearest single detached dwellings to the north

whoIsAffected.text: In spring and fall, shadows would reach some houses to the northeast from 1:18 pm. They would reach part of the townhouses to the east from 3:18 pm.

citations.quote: no shadows will be cast on the adjacent Neighbourhood lots until 1:18pm
There will be no shadow impacts on the townhomes to the east until 3:18pm

whoIsAffected.text: Trees: 39 private trees and 4 City street trees would be removed. The owner plans to plant 91 new trees on the site and 4 on the street.

citations.quote: this development would require the removal of 39 by-law protect privately-owned trees and 4 City-owned street trees
The submitted landscape plans propose the planting of 91 large-growing shade trees on the subject lands
the planting of 4 new trees within the adjacent road allowances

whoIsAffected.text: About 100 people came to a public meeting run by staff. Concerns included traffic, privacy, construction, height and trees.

citations.quote: Approximately 100 members of the public were in attendance
Concerns about possible impacts on trees as a result of excavation.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The new zoning comes with a hold. The new building cannot go ahead until the owner shows that sewer and water systems can handle it. Until then, only the existing uses are allowed.

citations.quote: Revisions are required to the Functional Servicing Report to demonstrate adequate servicing capacity
the subject site shall not be used for any purpose s other than those uses and buildings that currently exist on the site

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The draft zoning by-law was not included in the staff report. It was to be provided before the community council meeting.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: This page has not checked the zoning by-law that was later added to the item.

citations.quote: This attachment will be provided prior to the July 9, 2026, Scarborough Community Council Meeting.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Long-term care homes do not have to give land for parks or pay cash instead.

citations.quote: This proposed long-term care use is exempt from the parkland dedication requirement
Staff recommend that Council approve the Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment application.

committee.text: The community council held the public meeting. A motion to approve tied 3 to 3 and lost, so it went to City Council with no recommendation either way.

citations.quote: Scarborough Community Council forwards the item to City Council without recommendation as the motion to adopt the item lost on a tie vote.

council.text: City Council voted to adopt staff's recommendations and approved the Official Plan and zoning changes.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on July 29 and 30, 2026 with amendments.
That City Council adopt the following recommendations in the report (June 22, 2026) from the Director, Community Planning, Scarborough District:

whatHappensNext.text: Two by-laws have been passed for this item: 1222-2026 and 1223-2026.

Details such as wind protection at the outdoor garden and transit passes for staff are to be settled in a later step called Site Plan Control. The owner had not yet applied for it when the report was written.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record gives no dates for that step.

citations.quote: A Site Plan application has not been submitted.
will work with the applicant through the Site Plan application process to secure this along with other potential TDM measures
